region: DataFeel Dot contact surface — rest-associated profile

loci.basis: NTC thermistor at contact surface. Distal skin temperature rises slightly at sleep onset as core body temperature decreases (Van Someren, 2006). Gentle thermal modulation in this profile targets the 20–37 °C range without active warming above physiological neutral.

Normalised time-of-day (0.0 = midnight, 1.0 = midnight). Host-supplied raw clock phase; not measured by the device. Used as the clock source for the Origin-derived L-rest locus. Not directly used as an ABR interior locus in V0.4.

Cyclic trapezoidal rest schedule derived from the host clock. Wraps across midnight. Rises from 0 to 1 between 19:00 (phase 0.792) and 21:00 (phase 0.875). Peaks at 1.0 from 21:00 through midnight to 03:00 (phase 0.125). Falls from 1 to 0 between 03:00 and 07:00 (phase 0.125–0.292). Zero from 07:00 to 19:00 (daytime gap). Cyclic: value at phase=0.0 equals value at phase=1.0 (both 1.0 at midnight). Replaces the V0.3 gate_inverted=true mechanism — the schedule itself expresses the night-preference, keeping gate_inverted=false for clarity.

170 Hz resonant actuator. Rest profile uses lower amplitude and longer pulse duration than the activity profile. Low-amplitude vibrotactile stimulation at 170 Hz may support mechanotransduction in superficial tissue without arousal-level sensory activation.

RGB red channel, ~626 nm. The photobiomodulation (PBM) literature documents local tissue effects of 600–700 nm light via cytochrome c oxidase activation, including increased ATP production and anti-inflammatory cytokine modulation (Hamblin, 2016; Karu, 2010). 626 nm is at the lower boundary of this window. This is a local tissue mechanism, distinct from the retinal circadian signalling pathway activated by blue light. Dim output in the rest profile avoids retinal stimulation while remaining within the documented PBM wavelength range.

relations.description: Thermal disturbance (A) drives haptic amplitude (R) gated by the declared rest profile (B = L-rest). During the rest schedule window (L-rest high, 21:00–03:00 peak, wrapping across midnight), thermal changes produce a gentler haptic response consistent with the rest profile envelope. At midday, L-rest is zero and haptic output is suppressed. Same gate as R-02 — both modalities are simultaneously expressed during the declared rest window.

Thermal disturbance (A) drives red optical output (R) gated by the declared rest profile (B = L-rest). During the rest schedule window (L-rest high, 21:00–03:00, wrapping across midnight), thermal changes produce dim red illumination within the PBM wavelength range. The same Origin gate as R-01 means haptic and optical outputs are simultaneously expressed during the biological night — the multimodal co-activity window complementary to the activity profile.

provenance: Robin Macomber, Metatron Dynamics, Inc. — 2026-10-21. V0.4 rest-associated profile. ABR operator with Origin-declared rest schedule interior locus. gate_inverted=false; night-preference expressed by schedule. Scientific basis in docs/verification_record.md.
